sections.content: How many people are "aircraft pilots and air traffic controllers"?

17,825 people

were counted on the census as "aircraft pilots and air traffic controllers" in England and Wales in March 2021.

Aircraft pilots and air traffic controllers navigate and pilot aircraft, prepare flight plans, authorise flight departures and arrivals, maintain radio, radar and/or visual contact with aircraft to ensure the safe movement of air traffic, and check, regulate, adjust and test engines and other equipment prior to take-off. They may also give flying lessons.

More men than women had this job

Among people working as "aircraft pilots and air traffic controllers" there were more men than women (90.1% compared with 9.9%).

This means "aircraft pilots and air traffic controllers" had a different proportion of men and women compared with the wider occupation group it falls within of "business and public service associate professionals".

Men made up 90.1% and women made up 9.9% of "aircraft pilots and air traffic controllers"
Across the whole working population, 52% were men and 48% were women.

Other jobs that had a similar proportion of men and women to "aircraft pilots and air traffic controllers" included:

  • hospital porters
  • bus and coach drivers
  • butchers

These are the occupations for which the proportion of men and women was most equally split:

  • quality assurance and regulatory professionals
  • chartered and certified accountants
  • conservation professionals

How old are people who do this job?

The largest age group of people who had this job were those aged 50 to 54 years. Of the whole working population 11.7% were aged 50 to 54 years. For people working as "aircraft pilots and air traffic controllers", 14.1% were in this age group.

The age group with the smallest proportion of people working as "aircraft pilots and air traffic controllers" was 16 to 19 years.

Other jobs that had a similar age profile to "aircraft pilots and air traffic controllers" included:

  • managers in storage and warehousing
  • production, factory and assembly supervisors
  • special and additional needs education teaching professionals

Select your age group to see the ten most popular occupations for your age

How many people do this job by disability status, employment type and area

Of people working as "aircraft pilots and air traffic controllers", 3.1% were disabled. This means people said they had a long-term condition that limited them "a little" or "a lot" in their day-to-day activities. The average for all occupations is 9.6%.

Disability is more common among people who are older. This occupation had more people aged between 30 and 49 years compared with the whole working population.

People with this job were more likely to work full-time than part-time (59.2% compared with 40.8%).

They are also more likely to be an employee (92.4%) than self-employed (7.6%).

The region of England and Wales with the highest percentage of people with this job was the South East. At a local level, the areas with the highest percentage of people in this occupation included Horsham, this is in the same region of the South East.
